citations.text: OpenEvo comparison of Pillow (2012), Barzilai and Chinn (2018, 2024) and Hanisch and Eirdosh (2023), 2026-11-18. A shared field concept proposed by the comparison; no source defines it.
Pillow, B. H. (2012). Children's discovery of the active mind: Phenomenological awareness, social experience, and knowledge about cognition. Springer.

en.general: Noticing and judging one's own mental activity or performance as it happens: whether one understands, remembers or is sure, how hard something is, and where a piece of information came from. Pillow proposes five aspects of cognition that a person can become aware of: informational content, informational source, feelings of effort or difficulty, feelings of certainty or uncertainty, and emotions linked to thinking.

examples: A child notices that they do not remember a word and says so.
A student notices partway through a simulation task that she is unsure of her prediction and says so.
nonExamples: Carrying out a memory strategy without any awareness of whether it works.
A teacher rating a pupil's performance from outside.
